name: Bistronomie
summary: A chef of a palace kitchen cooks at the price of a bistro. Yves Camdeborde opened La Régalade in Paris in 1992 with a fixed menu, honest produce, regional dishes and big portions, in a plain room with no linen and no ceremony.

philosophy.core_thesis: Good cooking does not need a palace: a trained chef can serve fine produce and exact technique in a simple room at a fair price.
design_principles: Fix a menu of three courses at a low price, with a choice of a few dishes for each course.
Write the menu on a blackboard, and change it with the market.
Cook the dishes of the French provinces with the skill of a hotel kitchen: confit, terrine, braise and stew.
Serve a generous portion that fills a hungry guest.
Put a terrine or a pot of rillettes on the table at the start, and let the guests help themselves.
Use cheap cuts and offal with care: cheek, trotter, tongue and shoulder.
Plate on a plain plate or in the cooking pot, and use no formal service.
Seat guests close together in a room with a bar, bare tables and a short wine list.
anti_patterns: A white tablecloth and a waiter in a jacket
A tiny portion on a large plate
A long tasting menu at a high price
A dish made with foam, gel or liquid nitrogen
A menu that does not change with the market
A garnish of micro herbs placed with tweezers

plating.composition: A generous mound of food on a plain plate or in a small cast-iron pot, with the sauce around it and the garnish alongside.
plating.plate: A white or cream plate of 250 to 280 mm, a plain bowl or a small cast-iron casserole of 160 to 200 mm.
plating.portion: A main piece of 180 to 250 g with 150 g of garnish; the plate is about 75 per cent full.
plating.height: The food stands 30 to 60 mm high in a loose mound; the sauce is a spoon of jus beside or under it.
rules: Serve a terrine in its jar or on a board with a knife, a pot of mustard and cornichons.
Set a braised cut in its own cooking pot, or on the plate with a spoon of its jus.
Add a vegetable garnish that cooks with the meat: onion, carrot, cabbage or beans.
Cut bread in thick slices and put it on the table.
Finish with a dessert in a bowl or a jar, such as a rice pudding or a cream.

pantry.rule: Buy produce of the French provinces and cheap cuts of the market; use butter, wine and the cooking juices for the sauce.

technique.bases: A veal or pork stock, a jar of duck fat, a salted pork terrine mix, a bottle of red wine for the braise and a pot of mustard.
technique.details: A terrine in a jar, a braise served in its pot, a crisp skin on a duck leg, a spoon of jus, a thick slice of country bread.

flavour.profile: Deep and savoury: the taste of roast, braise and confit, with wine, mustard, garlic and thyme.
flavour.balance: Salt and umami lead with fat; vinegar, cornichons and mustard give acid; sweet stays in the dessert and in the onion.
flavour.fat: Butter, duck fat and pork fat give about 40 to 50 per cent of the energy of a main dish.
flavour.seasoning: Salt and pepper in layers, thyme and bay in the pot, garlic and shallot early, a splash of vinegar or mustard at the end.

palette.strategy: Use warm browns, the amber of duck fat and the cream of the plate, with one fresh green.

service.format: A fixed price menu with a choice of dishes; the waiter brings the plates and the pots to the table, with no ceremony.
service.courses: Three courses at a lunch or a dinner, with a terrine at the start and a cheese or a dessert at the end.
service.tableware: Plain white plates, cast-iron pots, a jar for the terrine, a plain glass and paper or bare tables.
service.setting: A small neighbourhood room of 30 to 50 seats with a zinc bar, close tables and a chef in an open kitchen who also serves.

dishes.dish: Pork terrine served in its jar
Braised pork cheek with root vegetables

positive: terrine served in a glass jar
braised pork cheek in a cast-iron pot
confit duck leg with crisp skin
Paris neighbourhood bistro with zinc bar
negative: tiny portion on a large plate

evidence.title: Terrine de campagne at a farm inn

emotion.target_response: The warmth of a crowded table where the food is better than the room: loud, generous and relaxed.

use_cases: a menu for a Paris neighbourhood bistro
a food photograph of a braise in a cast-iron pot
a blackboard menu with a fixed price
avoid_when: the brief wants a formal white-linen service
the brief wants a small architectural plate
the brief wants a plant-only menu

modifiers.request: more formal, with a tasting menu
modifiers.how: Cut the portion, plate in the kitchen on a large white plate, and raise the number of courses.
Use the dishes and produce of one province and give the name of its producers.
